NDT training in Miami: how it works for Miami employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training for Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET to Miami employers and technicians, either as live online classes or onsite at your facility in Miami-Dade or Broward. Your employer's written practice governs certification: you complete classroom training, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test.

That model matters in South Florida because the local NDT workforce is spread across very different kinds of employer. A component repair station in Doral or Medley, an inspection contractor supporting fuel terminals at Port Everglades, a structural-steel fabricator working on high-rise projects in Brickell, and a power-generation contractor supporting outages at the coast each need technicians qualified to a written practice that fits their own work. There is no single "Miami NDT certificate". What travels with you is the training and experience record; what makes you certified is your employer signing off against its written practice after the exams.

Atlantis NDT does not run a physical training centre in Miami. Classroom theory is delivered live online, and practical sessions are run onsite at the employer's facility, on the employer's own equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight. For many Miami shops that is the more useful arrangement: technicians train on the exact flaw detector, yoke, penetrant family or eddy current instrument they will use on the job, and nobody loses a day to I-95 traffic. Request a Miami training quote and tell us the methods, levels and head-count you need.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Miami

Every course below follows the SNT-TC-1A structure: method theory, the codes and procedures a technician will work to, equipment calibration, technique, and interpretation against acceptance criteria. Level I courses concentrate on performing set-ups and recording results under supervision; Level II courses add interpretation, evaluation and reporting against the applicable code; Level III preparation covers the basic, method and specific examinations. The minimum training hours and experience for each level are set in your employer's written practice; see our training requirements matrix for the SNT-TC-1A reference figures rather than relying on numbers quoted on third-party sites.

MethodLevelsWhat Miami employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepThickness surveys on terminal tanks and piping, weld inspection on structural steel for commercial towers, bond and lamination checks on marine structuresHigh-school level maths; Level II requires Level I training and experience per written practice
PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepWeld volumetric inspection where RT is impractical on busy job sites, corrosion mapping on piping and tank floorsNormally UT Level II first
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepThick-section weld inspection on pressure equipment and fabricated componentsNormally UT Level II first
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepWeld radiography on piping and pressure vessels, casting inspection, film and digital interpretationRadiation safety training plus the state requirements in the regulators section below
MT (magnetic particle testing)I, II, III prepSurface crack detection on ferromagnetic aircraft parts in repair stations, structural welds, landing-gear componentsNone beyond employer requirements
PT (liquid penetrant testing)I, II, III prepNon-ferrous aircraft components, stainless marine fittings, weld surface inspectionNone beyond employer requirements
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld visual inspection on structural steel, pre-coating inspection, general acceptance inspectionNone beyond employer requirements
ET (eddy current testing)I, II, III prepBolt-hole and surface crack inspection on aircraft structure, conductivity checks, tubing inspectionBasic electrical theory helpful

How the methods map to South Florida work. The Miami International Airport area holds one of the densest clusters of aviation repair stations in the United States, particularly around Doral, Medley, Miami Springs and Hialeah, many of which support Latin American and Caribbean operators. In that world, ET and PT are daily methods, and MT covers steel components such as landing-gear parts. Many aerospace employers work to NAS 410 or equivalent customer schemes; Atlantis does not train to NAS 410, but SNT-TC-1A-based method training gives technicians the underlying knowledge, and employers can map it into their own scheme. Industrial employers along the Port Everglades and PortMiami corridors lean on UT thickness, VT and MT, while fabrication and construction work leans on VT and UT of welds to AWS D1.1.

If you are not sure which method to start with, most new technicians begin with PT and MT Level I and II because the equipment is inexpensive and the methods appear in almost every sector. UT follows, then PAUT or TOFD for those moving into advanced ultrasonics. Our NDT training overview lists every course, and Level III preparation is available for experienced Level IIs.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Miami, step by step

  1. Confirm the employer's written practice. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer, not a training company and not ASNT, certifies you. The written practice defines the levels, training hours, experience, exam content and passing grades. If your Miami employer does not yet have one, see the employer section below.
  2. Complete classroom training. Formal training in the method and level, covering theory, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Live online delivery counts as formal training where the written practice allows it. The training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method and level.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Hours performing the method under supervision of certified personnel, documented in a way your Level III will accept. Keep your log from day one; reconstructing experience later is where most delays happen.
  4. Pass the general examination. A written test on method principles, administered under the authority of the employer's Level III.
  5. Pass the specific examination. A written test on the codes, procedures and equipment your employer actually uses, for example the aviation maintenance manual procedures used in a repair station, or ASME and AWS requirements used by a fabricator.
  6. Pass the practical examination. Hands-on testing on real specimens with known discontinuities, graded by the Level III against a checklist. This cannot be done in a simulator or over video.
  7. Pass the vision examinations. Near-vision acuity annually and colour contrast differentiation, as the written practice specifies.
  8. Receive employer certification. The employer issues certification in writing for the method and level. It is valid while you work for that employer.
  9. Recertify. SNT-TC-1A recommends recertification on a defined interval, with continued competence and fresh vision tests in between. Moving to a new employer means that employer must certify you against its own written practice.

For a deeper explanation of each step see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Miami crews

Live online theory. Classroom modules are taught live by video with an instructor, question sessions and recorded exercises. Technicians in Kendall, Hialeah, Fort Lauderdale or Homestead join from home or from a training room at work. This suits repair stations running shift work, because theory sessions can be scheduled around hangar shifts. Details are on the online NDT training page.

Onsite practical at your facility. Hands-on sessions are delivered at the employer's premises, using the employer's equipment and representative specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight. For Miami employers this keeps the training specific: a repair station trains on its own eddy current probes and reference standards; a fabricator trains on its own weld joints and procedures.

Scheduling around the South Florida calendar. Hurricane season runs from June to November, and many Miami employers either accelerate or pause field work around storm threats. Onsite cohorts are planned with a fallback date so that a named storm does not cost you the programme. Industrial clients with planned outages or tank out-of-service windows can schedule training in the weeks before the outage so newly certified technicians are ready when the work starts. Ask about onsite training for your Miami crew; cohort and onsite quotes are usually returned within one business day.

Corporate programmes. Employers training several technicians across methods can combine theory, practical sessions, exam administration and written-practice support. See corporate NDT training.

Where NDT technicians work in Miami

Aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul. The largest single source of NDT work in Miami-Dade is aviation. Repair stations certificated under FAA Part 145 perform component, engine accessory, landing-gear and structural work, and their NDT is usually defined by the aircraft or engine manufacturer's inspection manual. Eddy current, penetrant and magnetic particle dominate. Employers typically ask for method-specific certification, experience with specific manufacturer procedures, and often certification to NAS 410 or a customer equivalent.

Ports and fuel terminals. PortMiami and Port Everglades handle cruise, cargo and, at Port Everglades, a large share of the region's petroleum products. Tank farms and terminal piping need UT thickness, VT and MT. Tank owners typically follow API standards for in-service inspection; Atlantis does not provide API 653 or API 570 inspector training, but the underlying UT and VT method training is SNT-TC-1A-based and fits the NDT side of that work.

Power generation. Florida Power & Light operates the Turkey Point site south of Miami, which includes nuclear and gas-fired units, along with other generating stations across South Florida. Outage NDT work covers piping, valves, heat exchangers and structural welds, generally under ASME Section V and Section XI-driven programmes set by the owner. Nuclear work carries its own additional qualification layers defined by the utility.

Construction, bridges and structural steel. Miami's high-rise construction and the region's highway and bridge programmes rely on structural steel welded to AWS D1.1 and, for bridges, AWS D1.5. VT, UT and MT of structural welds are the core methods. Since the 2021 Surfside collapse, Florida has tightened recurring building safety inspections; much of that work is structural engineering and concrete assessment rather than classic NDT, but employers in that space increasingly value technicians who understand inspection discipline and documentation.

Marine and yacht work. South Florida's yacht building, refit and marine repair businesses use UT thickness gauging, PT on stainless and aluminium fittings, and VT on welds. Class society requirements from ABS, DNV or Lloyd's Register may apply to commercial vessels; those are owner and yard requirements rather than personnel certification schemes Atlantis trains to.

Radiography licensing in Florida. Florida is an NRC Agreement State. The Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Radiation Control, licenses the use of radioactive material, including industrial radiography sources, under Chapter 64E-5 of the Florida Administrative Code. Radiographers working with sealed sources must meet radiation-safety training and radiographer certification requirements that sit alongside, not inside, SNT-TC-1A method certification. Field radiography also requires at least two qualified individuals present at temporary job sites. Check the current rules directly with the Bureau before planning RT work; Atlantis teaches RT method theory and interpretation, and your employer's radiation safety officer governs the licensing side.

Level III services and written practices for Miami NDT companies

Many small Miami employers, particularly newer repair stations and inspection start-ups, discover the written-practice gap during a customer audit. Under SNT-TC-1A you cannot certify anyone until a written practice exists and a Level III is responsible for examinations. Atlantis supports employers with:

  • Written practice development and review, tailored to your methods, levels and customer requirements. See written practice development.
  • Level III services: preparing and administering general, specific and practical examinations, reviewing procedures, and signing off technique sheets where appropriate.
  • Procedure writing for UT, PAUT, MT, PT, VT, ET and RT, referencing the codes your customers require.
  • Audit preparation, including a records check of training hours, experience logs, vision tests and certification letters.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance for managers who need to understand what the document requires. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

For aviation employers working under customer-specified schemes, we will tell you honestly where SNT-TC-1A support applies and where you need a scheme-specific provider. Book a Level III consultation for your Miami operation.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical exam is where most candidates lose confidence, especially in methods they do not use daily. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Miami technicians the aircraft hangar environment mirrors repair-station work, and the storage tank environment reflects terminal inspection at the ports.

The simulator is practice only. It helps you rehearse set-up sequences, scanning patterns and interpretation decisions, but it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens, and it does not count as on-the-job experience. Use it between onsite sessions and before your exam day.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examination design and Level III services, and supervises onsite practical delivery for employer cohorts.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Miami

How do I get NDT certified in Miami?

Find an employer that will certify you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice, or ask your current employer. Complete formal classroom training in the method and level, log supervised on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass the vision tests. The employer then issues your certification.

Can I take NDT training online in Florida?

Yes. Classroom theory can be delivered live online to technicians anywhere in Florida, where the employer's written practice accepts it. The practical part must be done hands-on with real equipment and specimens, which Atlantis delivers onsite at the employer's facility. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice and your existing UT Level I training and experience. SNT-TC-1A sets recommended minimum classroom hours and experience hours per level; our training requirements matrix lists them. The experience component usually takes longer than the classroom component.

Do I need a license for radiography in Florida?

Radioactive material use requires a licence from the Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Radiation Control, held by the employer. Individual radiographers must meet state radiation-safety training and certification requirements. Those are separate from SNT-TC-1A method certification, which you also need to interpret radiographs. Confirm the current requirements with the Bureau.

What does NDT training cost in Miami?

Pricing is quote on request, because it depends on the method, level, group size, whether practical sessions run onsite and whether exam administration and written-practice support are included. Cohort and onsite quotes are usually returned within one business day. Request a Miami training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Miami employers?

SNT-TC-1A-based certification is the most common framework for industrial NDT in the United States. Aviation employers frequently layer customer requirements such as NAS 410 on top, and some marine work references class society requirements. Ask the employer which scheme applies before you start.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Miami?

In aviation repair stations, eddy current and penetrant testing are the most used methods, with magnetic particle for steel components. In industrial and construction work, UT, VT and MT are the core. Many technicians hold PT and MT first, then add UT or ET.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Miami?

No. Atlantis delivers theory live online and practical sessions onsite at the employer's facility in the Miami area, under Level III oversight.

Can a Miami repair station use Atlantis for Level III services?

Yes, for SNT-TC-1A-based programmes: written practices, exam administration, procedure review and audit preparation. Where a customer requires a different scheme, we will say so plainly.

Can I prepare for the Level III exam from Miami?

Yes. Level III preparation is delivered live online and covers the basic, method and specific examinations. Mock questions are available, for example UT Level 2 practice questions.

What do NDT technicians earn in South Florida?

Pay varies widely by method, level, sector and travel. Rather than quote unreliable local figures, see our NDT salary guide for the factors that move pay.

How do onsite sessions work around hurricane season?

Onsite cohorts between June and November are planned with a fallback date, and theory modules continue online if field sessions must move. Ask us to plan a storm-season schedule.
